questions_visited.why_selected: Curated lesson evidence for the effect of mass on impact speed.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State no effect and explain it using common free-fall acceleration when air resistance is negligible.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Compare identical initial velocity, height and g rather than comparing weights alone.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Greater mass automatically means greater impact speed.
lesson_sections_informed: Why mass does not change the impact speed in this model

questions_visited.why_selected: Curated lesson evidence for vertical fall time from rest.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Isolate vertical motion and select the displacement-time equation.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Set vertical u to zero, use s = ut + 1/2 at^2, then rearrange for positive time.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using the aircraft's horizontal speed in a purely vertical calculation.
lesson_sections_informed: The three equations you already know

questions_visited.why_selected: Curated lesson evidence for vertical impact velocity after a calculated fall time.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Use v = u + at with the vertical quantities only.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Carry the time from the prior part into a signed constant-acceleration velocity calculation.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Reporting a speed where the question asks for a vertical velocity component.

questions_visited.why_selected: Outcome-linked falling-object calculation with an upward initial velocity and downward final velocity.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Choose a coherent sign convention and find a height without time.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as with signed u, v, a and s, then interpret negative displacement as a height below the release point.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Discarding velocity signs before setting the convention or treating a negative displacement as an impossible answer.
lesson_sections_informed: A dropped phone and a clear direction

questions_visited.why_selected: Outcome-linked follow-on that tests the same upward-positive convention.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Represent constant negative acceleration with a velocity-time line that crosses zero.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use the selected positive direction to assign start and end velocities.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating a zero velocity at the turning point as zero acceleration.
lesson_sections_informed: Boundary check for next-lesson handoff only; maximum-height and upward-motion teaching remains deferred to Lesson 10.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped evidence for the maximum-height condition and no-time equation.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Set vertical velocity to zero at the top, use vertical initial velocity, and calculate maximum height.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Take upwards positive, set v=0 and a=-g, then solve v^2=u^2+2as.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating acceleration as zero at maximum height or using the full launch velocity instead of a vertical velocity.
lesson_sections_informed: The crucial instant at maximum height

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped evidence showing time-to-top as an intermediate quantity in a longer route.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Find time to maximum height then combine perpendicular displacements.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use v=u+at vertically to find the stage time, then apply later component processing.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using the launch velocity after the maximum-height boundary or mixing component directions.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped evidence for upward and downward displacement signs around the zero-velocity instant.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Find starting height from signed areas above and below a velocity-time graph.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Split at v=0, calculate the upward and downward triangular displacements, then subtract to obtain starting height.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Adding areas as distances without signs or treating the maximum-height instant as zero acceleration.
lesson_sections_informed: The crucial instant at maximum height
